parsed.why: No trans criminalisation, no prison system, no documented visitor-facing restriction; but doctrinal hostility toward gender theory, no anti-discrimination law, no recognition, and no recourse mechanism documented.

Decriminalised, self-declared third gender, court recognition and active civil society; yet documented public/government-institution discrimination, physical and sexual harassment of visibly trans, rising political hate speech, thin enforcement.

State criminalises trans depiction as pornography and bans gender-reassignment propaganda; documented mass detentions, custody abuse, police beatings, data collection on LGBT people, hostile propaganda, no recourse, foreigners threatened with expulsion.

Decriminalisation and statutory discrimination ban are real positives, but shadow reports show implementation gap, no gender recognition, and a 2024 police attack with arbitrary detention and degrading treatment of a trans woman.

Administrative gender recognition, gender-identity discrimination law, bias penalties, marriage equality, openly gay head of government; residual gaps are unclassified bias incidents and microaggressions rather than state or universal exposure.
